fullPassage: The human perceptual system is designed to recognize objects under changing illuminations, situations, and contexts. It is extraordinarily adapted to a constantly changing world. To deal with this uncertainty, the brain uses not one, but multiple routes. If one is blocked, it takes another route. This immense flexibility of the brain to rely on changing cues, according to whatever is available, is known as vicarious functioning. It can be found in most biological systems. In extreme cases, only a few lines are sufficient, as when we recognize the face of a celebrity in caricatures made with just a few pencil strokes. Face recognition also functions even when parts of a face are covered and internal features such as eyes are hardly visible. In this case, the brain relies on external features such as hair and head shape. For instance, migrating birds fly thousands of miles and may rely on the stars to navigate. But if it's a cloudy day, they may instead rely on landmarks or their magnetic sense. Similarly, the brain can recognize a face by the shape of the eyes, nose, and mouth.

To deal with this uncertainty, the brain uses not one, but multiple routes. If one is blocked, it takes another route. This immense flexibility of the brain to rely on changing cues, according to whatever is available, is known as vicarious functioning. It can be found in most biological systems. In extreme cases, only a few lines are sufficient, as when we recognize the face of a celebrity in caricatures made with just a few pencil strokes. Face recognition also functions even when parts of a face are covered and internal features such as eyes are hardly visible. In this case, the brain relies on external features such as hair and head shape. For instance, migrating birds fly thousands of miles and may rely on the stars to navigate. But if it's a cloudy day, they may instead rely on landmarks or their magnetic sense. Similarly, <u>the brain can recognize a face by the shape of the eyes, nose, and mouth</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 부분이 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 뇌의 얼굴 인식은 오직 눈, 코, 입의 형태에만 의존한다
뇌는 상황에 따라 다양한 단서를 활용하여 유연하게 인식한다
얼굴의 눈, 코, 입은 인식에서 가장 신뢰할 수 없는 특징이다
조류의 항법 능력과 인간의 얼굴 인식 능력은 근본적으로 다르다

det.korean: 마지막 문장은 뇌가 조류처럼 상황에 따라 다양한 인식 수단을 사용한다는 것을 함축
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문불일치: '오직'이라는 제한은 뇌의 유연한 다경로 활용과 모순
✅ ② 함축의미: Similarly로 이어지며, 이주 새 예시처럼 뇌도 상황에 따라 다양한 단서(눈/코/입, 머리카락, 머리 형태)를 활용한다는 vicarious functioning의 핵심 ← 정답
❌ ③ 원문불일치: 눈, 코, 입은 유효한 인식 단서로 언급됨
❌ ④ 원문불일치: Similarly는 공통점을 강조하는 접속부사
